I'll read `scripts/slow.mjs` first to see what it does.
The file has two hot spots: `countPrimes` (trial division up to 60,000) and `dedupe` (`includes` on an array). I'll time each one separately without touching the repo.
`countPrimes` is the slow part. In my timing run it took about 556 ms, versus about 48 ms for `dedupe`.

`isPrime` in `scripts/slow.mjs` (lines 2–6) does trial division, checking every `i` from 2 up to `n - 1`. `countPrimes` (lines 7–11) calls it for every number below 60,000, so the total work grows roughly with the square of the limit. The `dedupe` function (lines 12–16) is also quadratic because of `out.includes`, but it runs on only 30,000 values with 9,000 unique results, so it costs far less.

I didn't change any files. The timings came from an inline copy of the same functions, not from running the script itself.
